text:
ryan: FYI escalation from Acme — their rerank requests are returning wildly off-range scores (examples include -1.2e6, +8.9e5) and sometimes all zeros. Also hitting occasional 413 on large batches and a couple 401s. Customer says UI flips results when the scores change.

maria: ack, thanks for raising. Can you paste the exact curl + payload they used and which model/version they called?

tom: tagging infra — 413 points to payload size limit. We shipped a batching limiter last week, could be related. Also want to see request ids for the 401s.

ryan: here's the curl they sent (redacted key):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{\n    "model": "rerank-xlarge-v2",\n    "queries": ["what is the refund policy?"],\n    "candidates": [ /* 2000 short docs */ ]\n  }'
```

ryan: they said they had ~2000 candidates in a single request to get one-shot ranking.

alice: quick context: our rerank endpoint returns raw scores/logits (not probabilities) by design. Clients expecting 0-1 probabilities will see negative values and large magnitudes. That said, magnitudes in the 1e6 range look like a numeric overflow or corrupted batch. Were they using an SDK that post-processes or casts types?

maria: @ryan can you also paste the response they saw (snippet) and the request_id header from the response?

ryan: response snippet:

```
{
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "scores": [ -1203456.5, 0, 234567.0, -inf, 0, 0 ],
  "status": "partial_failure"
}
```

tom: I pulled logs for req_0a1b2c3d — I see a 413 at the transport layer, then a retry that timed out, and a couple auth failures from different IPs (401). Looks like a client retried with rotated/expired key and also re-sent a truncated body in one attempt which produced 0s.

tom: log excerpt: 

```
[03:16:12 UTC] INGRESS req_0a1b2c3d size=1.9MB -> accepted
[03:16:13 UTC] ROUTER  req_0a1b2c3d -> shard-17 413 PayloadTooLarge
[03:16:14 UTC] CLIENT_RETRY req_0a1b2c3d -> auth=401 key_id=key_rot_22
[03:16:15 UTC] WORKER   req_0a1b2c3d -> compute fail: overflow in accumulation -> produced INF
```

maria: summary of likely causes: 1) very large batch -> partial truncation/413; 2) retries with rotated/invalid key -> transient 401; 3) numeric overflow on worker when candidate count extreme -> INF/-1e6 style values.

maria: action items for support: please ask customer to retry with smaller batches (<=256 candidates), include header X-Request-ID if they set it, and send us a full raw response + request_id if the issue persists. Also confirm they treat scores as logits and apply softmax if they need probabilities.

ryan: customer tried limiting to 100 candidates. Results now look like normal logits (range ~ -5 .. +4). They were previously treating scores as probabilities, so the UI showed strange rankings. They want a user-friendly fix so product teams don't misinterpret output.

alice: I'll draft a short snippet for docs & SDK: show how to convert logits -> probabilities client-side: softmax(scores) and note numerical-stability trick (subtract max before exp). Recommend adding a convenience helper in our JS/Python SDKs that returns probs if requested.

tom: infra follow-up: I'll add a guard in the worker to detect extreme absolute values (|score| > 1e5) and surface a warning in the response that computation overflow/abnormality occurred. Also add metric for frequency of INF/NaN in rerank outputs.

maria: we should also surface a clearer 413 error message linking to the batch-size limits doc and recommending chunking, and update our rate-limit docs to advise exponential backoff/retry with new key checks.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15 03:02 UTC — routing-limiter v2 rolled out to prod

ryan: I'll follow up with Acme with repro steps (reduced batch + header) and the request ids. Thanks all, I'll close the loop once they confirm. :thumbsup:

maria: nice triage. If Acme still sees large magnitudes after these steps, escalate to eng-ml with the request ids so they can replay raw traces.

alice: drafting docs blurb now, will paste here when ready.

ryan: sending the customer the guidance and the temporary workaround.
